title: Conditions and logical operators
goal: Choose a branch by priority and guard a calculation with a condition evaluated before it.

prerequisites.text: Read a validated integer from one line.
Know why remainder with a zero divisor is invalid.

terms.title: Predicate
terms.definition: A check whose result is true or false. In C a condition with value 0 is false.

terms.title: Short-circuit evaluation
terms.definition: && skips its right operand after a false left operand. || skips the right after a true left operand.

terms.title: Branch priority
terms.definition: The order of tests in if / else if. The first matching branch runs.

sections.title: Why it matters
paragraphs: A maintenance marker should fall exactly on an interval boundary. A zero interval cannot be used as the divisor of the remainder operation, so test the interval first.
&& and || evaluate their left operand first. For example, a != 0 && x % a == 0 attempts the remainder only after checking a. ! changes zero to 1 and any nonzero value to 0.
Separate if statements are checked independently. An if / else if / else chain selects one result when several rules can apply.
The stock states form a decision tree. Check that the pack is usable, then check whether any stock is available. Test the remainder only in the branch with a positive pack size.

sections.title: Checking a maintenance marker
paragraphs: distance is 12 and interval is zero. Predict whether 12 % 0 is evaluated.
Trace the listing with interval = 5 and interval = 6. For each value, say whether the right operand is evaluated and which branch is taken.
steps: && skips its right operand after a false left operand.
The false condition selects the else branch.

sections.title: The guard comes before calculation
paragraphs: Swapping the operands can accidentally attempt remainder with a zero divisor. Reason through that unsafe variant without running it.
Both && and || need two operands. If && is followed immediately by ), Clang reports that it expected an expression.

sections.title: Priority when multiple rules match
paragraphs: Consider 0 0 in the packing task. It matches “no stock” and “invalid pack size”. The contract gives the invalid size priority.
Reading zero successfully differs from a parsing error. read_integer reports a status separately, so zero does not signal failure.
For each trace, mark the first true branch and separately note whether the remainder is ever calculated. With two zeroes the test checks error priority, before any grouping rule is considered.

selfcheck.prompt: Which edit removes the protection from a zero interval?
feedback: The remainder becomes the left operand.

selfcheck.prompt: With stock = 0 and pack = 0, which two tests are true and why must invalid come first?
selfcheck.feedback: Both tests for zero are true. A bad pack size takes precedence. Testing stock first would print empty for an invalid request.

practice.title: Classify stock for packing
practice.task: Read two lines, stock and pack size, each from 0 to 100. Print invalid for invalid input or a pack size of zero. Print empty for zero stock. Otherwise print ready if stock divides exactly and partial if it leaves a remainder. Ignore input after the two records.
practice.hint: The first two branches make % safe in the remaining branches. Add an else if for exact division before the final else.
criteria: 18 and 6 give ready. 19 and 6 give partial.
0 and 0 give invalid. 0 and 7 give empty.
Print exactly one line in each branch.

steps.expected: An invalid pack size takes priority over stock status.

steps.action: Add a branch for zero remainder.
steps.why: Earlier checks exclude a zero divisor.

steps.action: Compare 0 0 and 0 7 using two lines of input.
steps.expected: Explain the different outcomes through priority.

exercises.title: Choose a neighbouring boundary case
exercises.task: With a pack size of 100, find two adjacent valid stock counts for which the answer changes.

cases.label: Invalid pack takes priority over empty stock

teaching.scene: A technician checks whether a marker is on a service interval. The interval is sometimes zero. Trace which parts of the condition actually run and predict the one resulting message.

predict.prompt: The sample has distance 12 and interval 0. What happens on the left of &&, is the remainder evaluated, and which line appears?
predict.answer: interval > 0 is false. && finishes evaluating the condition before `%`, so no division takes place. The else branch prints inspect.

apply.prompt: A packer tests four runs, one number per input line: stock 0 with size 4, stock 7 with size 4, stock 8 with size 4, and stock 0 with size 0. In which runs is the remainder calculated and what does each print?
apply.answer: For 0 and 4, print empty without computing a remainder. For 7 and 4, the remainder is 3 and the result is partial. For 8 and 4, the remainder is 0 and the result is ready. For 0 and 0, the size check wins, so it prints invalid without doing remainder arithmetic.

practice.strategy: Order the states from rejected input through ordinary grouping. Pick one input for each branch and check that each run prints a single line.
practice.diagnosis: If 18 with 6 gives partial, inspect the zero-remainder check on nonempty data. If 0 with 0 gives empty, the empty-stock branch is firing too early.

syntax.explanation: && evaluates its left operand first. The right side runs only when the left side is true.
syntax.mistake: Operand order matters. Guard divisor before using it with `%`.
